title: fix(pm): ci-failure resolves a red lane's Lane verdict to its red gates' own commands
body:
Fixes #23223
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

Since #23191, every gate step of a `Lint · *` / `Type Check · *` lane runs under `continue-on-error: true`. A red gate's jobs-API `conclusion` is therefore `success`, so the only failed step of a red lane is its last one, `Lane verdict`. `scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` resolved that step name through `stepBodies`. The name exists once per lane, so the `substitute` block printed `node scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` 12 times. Run locally, that command exits 3 and reproduces nothing.

Now, when the failed step is `Lane verdict`, the tool reads the red gate names from the verdict's own sentences (`gate step "NAME" (id ID) failed`). It resolves each name through `stepBodies` to that gate's own `run:` block. The `substitute` block prints those commands. The verdict's own command is never offered.

Only one file changes: `scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` and its `--self-test`. Nothing under `.github/workflows/**`, `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` or `.claude/**` is touched.

- `classifyAnnotation` gains one kind, `lane-verdict`. It recognises the five sentences that `lane-verdict.mjs`'s `renderVerdict` writes as error annotations: `red`, `unread`, `did-not-run`, `fail-fast` and `refusal`. For `red`, it keeps the gate name and id. Everything else still classifies as before. `assertionStatus` and `verdictOf` read the new kind as content, the same as the old `other`, so the exit table does not move.
- `readLaneVerdict` takes the union of those sentences from two sources, deduplicated: the check-run's annotations and the job log's error lines. The log is already fetched for this family, so it costs no extra request. GitHub's documentation says one step can create only a limited number of error annotations. A lane with more red gates than that limit would name only some of them in the annotations; the log names them all. That limit is NOT measured here, and the union makes the result independent of it.
- `resolveFailedStep`: every step except `Lane verdict` resolves by its own name, unchanged. For `Lane verdict`, `repro` holds the red gates' hits, each carrying `gate: { name, id }`, and `laneVerdict` holds the full reading. Both appear in `--json`.
- `renderSubstitute` is the old inline `sayRepro`, now a pure function so the self-test can pin the printed lines. When the verdict names no runnable red gate, it says why, in one of three ways:
  - **Names no red gate** (an unread gate, a gate that did not run, a fail-fast step, or a refusal): it lists what the verdict did name and says that no gate command reproduces this red.
  - **NOT READ**: the annotations call failed and no log was read.
  - **UNRESOLVED**, loudly: no sentence matches a known shape. The wording may have changed, or the verdict died before printing. It never falls back to printing the verdict command.
- `stepBodies` now filters a new `workflowSteps` scan. The output is identical, and the existing pins still hold.

## Proof on the measured sample

Run 38373082677 (PR head `5301220aa`), check-run / job 115214618941, `node scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs --run 38373082677`. The tool has no `--job` flag, so `--run` was used.

Before, on `main` at `197fbe2c04`:

```text
    failed step  #68  Lane verdict
    ...
    substitute   run the failing step locally — it prints the same assertion:
      from .github/workflows/lint.yml, step "Lane verdict" (run:)
        node scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs
      (the same pair, 12 times in all)
```

After, on this branch:

```text
    lane verdict #68 "Lane verdict" judges this lane's gates; it is not one, and its own
                 command reproduces nothing (run locally it exits 3). What it named:
                   RED       "Docs anchors resolve to real headings" (id docs-anchors-resolve-to-real-headings)
                 1 red gate(s); each one's OWN command is the substitute below.
    substitute   run the failing step locally — it prints the same assertion:
      from .github/workflows/lint.yml, red gate "Docs anchors resolve to real headings" (id docs-anchors-resolve-to-real-headings), named by step "Lane verdict" (run:)
        pnpm check:doc-anchors
        node scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs --self-test
        node scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs
```

`diff before after` shows only three changes: the two `other` heads for that sentence become `lane-verdict`, and the substitute block above changes. The other three failing checks on that sha render byte-identical. The walk still exits 2 (UNDETERMINED) both times, because none of the four failing checks carries a file-anchored assertion. The exit table is unchanged on purpose.

## Self-test, and ablation that proves it can fail

A new battery, `Lane verdict: the red gates, not the verdict (#23223)`, has 22 cases. The `stepBodies / resolveStep` battery goes from 8 to 9 cases, and the battery floor from 14 to 15.

The battery imports `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` and drives its real `judgeLane` and `renderVerdict`. The parser is therefore pinned to what the producer actually prints, so a wording change there turns this battery red. No rendered line is printed: they are workflow commands, and this self-test runs on a runner.

The cases pin the card's three requirements:
- N red gates give N gate commands, and the verdict command is never printed.
- An all-success lane with a red verdict (a roster mismatch: a gate with `continue-on-error` and no `id:`) says it names no red gate. It does not resolve to nothing, and it does not read as "resolves to no `run:` block".
- On a pre-#23191 head, a failed gate step whose conclusion is `failure` resolves exactly as before, line for line.

The cases also cover the measured specimen, all five sentence shapes, the UNRESOLVED and NOT READ cases, the log/annotation union, a red gate that is missing from the local tree, and a gate name containing quotes and parentheses. A live pin requires that every step in the real workflow tree that runs the verdict is named `Lane verdict` (12 of them today). A lane that renames its verdict step therefore turns the self-test red instead of silently bringing the defect back.

Ablations were run on committed `77480b13ce` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. In each leg the anchor hit 1 to 0, the blob changed, and the restore was proven blob == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`:

| leg | mutation | self-test | cases red |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `resolveFailedStep` stops treating `Lane verdict` specially | exit 1 | 8 (N→N, substitute, roster mismatch, UNRESOLVED, NOT READ, missing gate) |
| 2 | the `red` sentence pattern no longer matches | exit 1 | 8 (specimen, real-renderer parse, quoted name, N→N, union, missing gate) |
| 3 | every other step resolves to no command | exit 1 | 2 (the two pre-A1 pins) |

My first leg-1 run crashed the harness on `r.gate.name` instead of reporting the failure. Two accessors are now null-safe, so a regression is reported rather than thrown (`77480b13ce`).

## Local gates, at `77480b13ce`

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran FILE` reports 30 derived, 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, with an exit code recorded for every one (all 0). That count includes `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` (EXIT=0, 397 s), `node scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs --self-test`, `node scripts/check-self-test-workflow-commands.mjs` (its end-to-end case runs this self-test and finds no runner-parsed line), `pnpm check:nul-bytes` and `pnpm check:entry-guard`.
- The rule that an edited tool's own test suites are owed: `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --self-test` (EXIT=0, 500 assertions; it reads this file's unchanged `PROXY_REARM_GUARD` line).
- eslint, narrowed to this one file:
  - `pnpm lint` is `eslint . --no-inline-config`, and `eslint --print-config scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` resolves a config for it, so the file is inside the lint population.
  - `--no-inline-config --format json scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` reports 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - The printed config has no `parserOptions.project` (`eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting), and the two rules that apply are per-file syntactic rules. So this diff cannot change the verdict for any file it does not touch.
- No changeset: `scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing (`skip-changeset`).

## Acceptance notes

- A gate name that appears in more than one workflow step still resolves to every hit. This is the existing documented `resolveStep` behaviour ("picking one would be a silent guess"). One example: `Sweep the built closure for vanished declarations` is a step in `ci.yml` build-core and in two `lint.yml` lanes, and the two lint steps share one `id:`. So the annotation's id cannot narrow it either. Narrowing by job would need a mapping from job display names to job ids, which is outside this card.
- The card's optional `references/platform-readings.md` half is not in this PR: it is a governed `.claude/**` path, and the claim leaves it to #23201 or a skills card. The platform reading it would record is quoted in this file's header instead: under `continue-on-error`, a red gate's API `conclusion` is `success` and only the steps-context `outcome` is `failure`.
- The `Lint & Repo Gates` aggregator row (`Verify every lint lane succeeded`) still offers its own aggregator script as the substitute. It names the red lane in an annotation (lint lane `lint-repo-tooling` concluded `failure`), and the lane's own row, fixed here, carries the gate commands. Noted only.
